# ADR Kit

> ADR Kit is a command-line tool for Architecture Decision Records (ADRs).
> It turns architecture decisions into plain Markdown files with a
> machine-checkable lifecycle: decisions are durable records, proposals are
> ephemeral drafts. Built for humans and AI coding assistants.

## Links

- Repository: https://github.com/luochang212/adr-kit
- npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/adr-kit
- CLI reference: https://github.com/luochang212/adr-kit/blob/main/docs/cli.md
- Record format: https://github.com/luochang212/adr-kit/blob/main/docs/record-format.md
- Workflow guide: https://github.com/luochang212/adr-kit/blob/main/docs/workflow.md
- Changelog: https://github.com/luochang212/adr-kit/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md

## Quick start

Requires Node.js 20.19 or later.

```bash
npm install -g adr-kit
cd your-project
adrkit init --tools claude
adrkit decide "Use SQLite for session storage" --raised-by human --decided-by human
adrkit validate
```

`--raised-by` and `--decided-by` are both required on `decide` and `accept`,
one value each per record: `raised-by` is who put the decision on the table,
`decided-by` whose judgment settled it. For `decided-by`, use `human` when a
person determined the direction (they stated it, changed a proposal into what
shipped, or you are recording one they made earlier), `agent` when it came from
the agent's own judgment, including when a person only let it through. The CLI
neither infers nor verifies either; who redirected or approved belongs in the
record body.

To record a decision that still needs review, use `adrkit propose "<title>"`
(a draft in `adr/.drafts/`), then `adrkit accept "<title>" --raised-by human --decided-by human`
to promote it or `adrkit reject "<title>"` to discard it.

## Key facts

- Records are plain Markdown; the parser and validator are the format
  contract.
- Validation failures are success signals: a draft that `accept` refuses to
  promote is missing a required section.
- Drafts carry dates; decision numbers are assigned only at accept time.
- A decision may carry an optional `## Deliberation` appendix, the design tree
  behind it as a nested list where a follow-up question is nested under the
  node that raised it; `adrkit tree <name>` renders it as text, `--mermaid` as
  a graph, or `--html` as an offline interactive card tree.
- The whole decision set renders as an offline decision map with
  `adrkit graph --html`: one self-contained file with supersede and reference
  edges grouped by creation date, marking the decisions that carry a
  deliberation tree and linking each node to its record.
- `adrkit-grill` questions and records decisions; `adrkit-visualize` renders
  existing trees or the whole decision map and opens HTML in the default browser
  on request, with a file link and a file-only opt-out.
- Rejection is not a record: it lives in the winner's `Alternatives
  considered`.
- AI tool integrations (`adrkit init --tools`): claude, codex, cursor,
  github-copilot, agents (generic .agents/). Installs agent skills and
  slash-command files.
- Works alongside spec-driven tools like OpenSpec: OpenSpec tracks what is
  being built; ADR Kit records why a direction was chosen.
- License: MIT. Single runtime dependency: yaml.
